_comment: 2026-08-09. Same hour trace as mix_dyn60_short_m123 with two changes.
1. Arrival band 25-75 -> 10-45 req/s. The workload got heavier when the
per-worker prompt duplication was removed on 2026-08-08, and EXP-70
then measured the knee at 28.1 req/s for FluidServe v0.2 and 18.2 for
llm-d. On the old band 93% of the hour sat above our knee and 100%
above llm-d's, so the trace measured how aggressively each policy
refuses rather than how it routes, and the arrival rate never crossed
the knee in either direction. On this band the rate is above our knee
47% of the minutes and below it the rest, which is the condition the
trace exists to create.
2. chat num_conversations 1,000 -> 10,000, matching the static configs.
At 1,000 the pool gives 3,451 requests against 77,032 chat arrivals,
so each prompt would return every 2.7 minutes, which is close enough
to the engine's KV residence (about 1 minute) to inflate the prefix
cache hit rate. At 10,000 it returns every 26.9 minutes.
Replay that remains, and why it is left alone: chat 2.23x at 26.9 min
between copies, deep research none, swe 6.59x at 9.1 min. The engine
holds about one minute of prompt content per instance and the scheduler's
own prefix index about 2.8 minutes, so a copy arriving 9 minutes later
finds neither. This is a different thing from the defect fixed on
2026-08-08, where 12 copies arrived within 2.1 seconds. Enlarging the swe
transcript would trade the replay for a worse problem: its records are
consecutive calls of one agent job, so a 13,218-record build has 98.9%
structural prefix sharing against this 1,500-record stride sample's
78.9%, which would make the class almost entirely cached.
Derived from mix_dyn60_short_m123_slofair.json (plan /work/traces/dynamic/canonical/dyn60_short_m123.csv, chat pool 1000).
